citations.assessment: The bench example names Pappa bar Abba, and Rashi explicitly glosses his large build. The root’s clipped “to Ravina” is retained and separately qualified.
Heilprin reports a singular questioner. The checked Bavli expressly gives members of the household as the questioners.
Pappa cites the daughter-in-law of Pappa bar Abba’s household. The source is not a direct speech by Pappa bar Abba himself.
Names the household in an inquiry from Rav Pappa to Rava.

Two witnesses preserve the same question with different speakers. Shevuot gives Rav Sheshet and Rabbah bar Shmuel, whereas the Epistle gives Rav Pappa bar Abba and Rabbah bar Shaul. Heilprin’s Bava Metzia citation remains separately qualified.
Pappa bar Abba’s sons challenge Ravina.
Sons of Rav Pappa bar Abba ask ordinary Rav Pappa the Shabbat question.

holds.reason: The bench passage attributes the illustration to ordinary Rav Pappa and does not name Ravina. The separately cited Yoma attests a challenge from the sons to Ravina. Keep the clipped root wording.
The Bava Metzia description names plain Rav Pappa in a euphemistic comparison and does not explicitly name bar Abba. Exact wording in Heilprin’s witness and any identification remain qualified.
